dispositions.claim_text: “One Who carries the Discus called Sudarśana.” The term Su — Darsana means “that which gives the auspicious vision." The śāstras attribute to this Discus — Divine the representation of the human mind.
dispositions.reason: Cakrī means discus-bearer; su+darśana analyzes the weapon’s separate name and mind symbolism interprets it.

dispositions.claim_text: The traditional meaning is, of course, "One Who has the 'wheel of the chariot' as His weapon." This means the Discus which already has been mentioned in this very Stanza as cakrī.
dispositions.reason: Rathāṅga ‘chariot wheel/discus’+pāṇi ‘hand’ supports one with wheel in hand. Weapon and cakrī cross-reference are contextual.
